articles.title: Werwulf Director Robert Eggers Reveals New Details About His 'Hell-Like' Medieval Horror Film
articles.summary: Director Robert Eggers reveals eerie new details about Werwulf, his upcoming medieval horror film starring Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe and Lily-Rose Depp.
articles.body:
“After Nosferatu, I kind of said, ‘Let me try to write the scariest thing I can write.’ I don't know that I did that, but I definitely wrote the darkest thing,” writer-director Robert Eggers told the press at a promotional event Friday for his upcoming horror film, Werwulf. And based on the roughly 20 minutes of select footage I saw from the film, Werwulf indeed has all the makings of being Eggers’ darkest and scariest movie yet.

Werwulf follows a 13th-century farmer (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), simply referred to as Man, who is cursed as a werewolf. Lily-Rose Depp plays his wife and the mother of his children, while Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson, and Jack Morris play a trio of wolf hunters on a mission to kill the werewolf.

Eggers kicked the event off by screening the opening scene of Werwulf, a dialogue-free nighttime sequence. The howling of wolves can be heard over a black screen. Then the Man’s face is revealed. He is foaming at the mouth and in great pain. The Man sprints naked through the woods and enters an empty home. Inside, he suffers wild convulsions in the moonlight and growls in agony. He writhes on the floor, and eventually ends up in the shadows where his transformation continues unseen. Taylor-Johnson performed all these body-bending movements himself (save for one shot that could not be accomplished practically), and it was truly a wild sight to behold. Eggers stressed, though, “that is not the set piece werewolf transformation.”

“I think werewolf movies are a difficult genre. And I think sometimes even if it's a great werewolf movie, it's hard to believe that your dad's turning into a werewolf or your next door neighbor who's a high school basketball player is turning into a werewolf,” Eggers said. But a period werewolf movie “really helps ground you and ground the audience. At least that's the intention.”

While I won’t give blow-by-blow details of the other scenes in order to avoid spoilers, the additional footage showed: aspects of the Man’s youth; hints at how and why he ended up cursed; the arrival of three wolf hunters at the Man’s home in the middle of the night to violently enlist his help in hunting down a werewolf; and the Man and the hunters’ journey to find a strange old woman who may know a thing or two about werewolves.

Eggers did copious amounts of research on England in the 13th century for the screenplay, he co-wrote with his The Northman collaborator, Sjón. The film’s dialogue is in Middle English, although it’s been altered by dialect coach William Conacher to make it more comprehensible for the modern ear. Eggers also worked with two Middle English scholars at Oxford University, Eleanor Baker and Daniel Wakelin , who helped make the dialogue more period accurate.

Although the dialogue is in Middle English, Eggers said that Werwulf “was designed to be kind of like a silent movie. You don't need to understand what anyone's saying to understand the movie because you're with everyone on an emotional level, particularly Aaron and his family.”

Eggers’ fascination with werewolf lore goes back to this youth. “The historical werewolves that I had read about starting in high school, they were doing things that were so taboo and hard for anyone to wrap their mind around because it was so extreme that the culture that they existed in said, ‘You can't be a human, you must be a werewolf.’ So it was going to be very dark and very primal subject matter,” the filmmaker said.

“I wanted to make it in England and because Edward I was trying to protect the wool trade around the time of this movie, he set a campaign to exterminate all the wolves. Actually, Willem's character is based on a real person who did such a good job that in another 200 years there were not wolves in England. So without wolves, you don't have werewolf lore. So if I was going to set it in England, it had to be this early in history around 1300. And that was even more exciting, because the world would be so primitive and so visceral and primal that that would make this all the more dark and brutal.”

The world of Werwulf is so dark and brutal that Eggers’ said cinematographer Jarin Blaschke texted him after he first read the script and asked, "’Does this take place in hell?’ And it needs to be hell for Aaron. And I think some medievalists would be annoyed that I'm kind of clinging to the stereotype of the Middle Ages being so muddy and dirty and rainy and miserable, but it needs to be so muddy, and rainy, and dirty, and miserable, and shit-covered, and it does need to be hell. But again, I always find that doing the research about the period, you learn stuff that makes it more interesting and more specific. And for this particular movie, more hell-like.”

Audiences will discover for themselves just how hell-like Werwulf is when it opens in theaters Christmas Day.

articles.title: John Goodman, Laura Bailey, and Ian Alexander to Star in HBO's The Last of Us Season 3
articles.summary: Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series.
articles.body:
Emmy-winning actor John Goodman, prolific voice talent Laura Bailey, and returning star Ian Alexander have been cast in the third (and possibly final) season of HBO’s The Last of Us series.

As revealed on September 26 — the day the Cordyceps infection ravaged humanity in The Last of Us universe — the show’s third season will feature three big talents, two of whom are making their return to Naughty Dog’s flagship zombie franchise.

Perhaps most surprisingly, John Goodman has been slated to play a character named Joey, a figure who wasn’t in the original games. Joey is joined by another character named Paco, who will be played by Ian Alexander; the two are described as a “friendly duo who dub themselves ‘Heroes of the Highway.’” Alexander notably played Lev in The Last of Us Part 2 , a young boy who Abby helps rescue from the Seraphite cult.

The Last of Us Season 2 Episode 1: TV Show vs Game Comparison

The Seraphites will play a part in season 3, as Laura Bailey is set to play Elizabeth, one of the cult’s leaders. Bailey is also a returning actor to the franchise, having famously voiced Abby in The Last of Us Part 2 alongside Alexander.

With the Seraphites being included in the third season and Alexander playing a new character, it stands to reason that another person will be playing Lev, most likely because Alexander has aged out of the role.

These two aren’t the only actors from the original games who have been included in HBO’s screen adaptation; Ashley Johnson and Troy Baker also played characters in The Last of Us Season 1, with Johnson playing Ellie’s mother in a harrowing birth scene and Baker playing James, a member of Baker’s villainous group.

Johnson and Baker famously provided the voice and motion performances for Ellie and Joel in both of The Last of Us Games, so it’s not surprising that Bailey and Alexander are also showing up in some way.

HBO’s The Last of Us series is expected to end with this forthcoming season, which will air in 2027. In a September interview with Deadline, the Chairman and CEO of HBO and Max Content, Casey Bloys, said he “thinks [showrunner] Craig [Mazin] has planned it as the final season.”

Bloys has been hinting at this since January, saying in another Deadline interview that “it certainly seems that way, but on decisions like that, we will defer to the showrunners. So you can ask them.”

With the games’ creator, Niel Druckmann, having left the project after Season 2, the future of HBO’s show is looking uncertain — but with talent like Alexander, Bailey, and Goodman on board, there’s bound to be some fantastic performances in store. We just hope they don’t tear our hearts apart like Nick Offerman did in the first season.

articles.body:
In the aftermath of yet another price hike , Disney has revealed next month’s streaming lineup for both Disney+ and Hulu.

Why are we talking about both streaming services at the same time? Over the past year, Disney+ and Hulu have been slowly merging their libraries . They also cost about the same as a bundle as they would as individual standalone services, presumably by design.

If you’re debating whether to stick with the more expensive subscriptions, here’s a look ahead at what you’ll be getting out of it next month. The topline? We’re looking at a new MCU series, tons of ABC show premieres, and plenty of Halloween specials.

Highlights Coming to Disney+ and Hulu Next Month

One of the most anticipated TV streaming premieres is a new season of Ryan Murphy’s fever dream, American Horror Story. Plenty of cast members have returned for the hauntingly significant 13th season, including Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, and Emma Roberts. In other words, expect some wacky crossovers of characters and plotlines from previous seasons.

While the first three episodes premiered on FX in late September, they won’t be coming to Hulu until the start of October. Time to get spooky.

The Hunger Games movies have moved around streaming services quite a bit over the years. While the full franchise is already available to Netflix subscribers, Hulu will also be getting the full movie marathon this October. Having all of the movies in one place is a great chance to catch up on or rewatch the dystopian saga ahead of a new prequel movie, Sunrise on the Reaping .

The biggest Disney+ premiere of the month comes from the MCU side of things. VisionQuest is a new series that follows up 2017’s WandaVision, one of the most acclaimed Marvel projects in the streaming era. While we already know the series will bring back some old-school Marvel characters , cast members have been close-lipped about whether we’ll see the return of the Scarlet Witch herself .

Between last year’s Weapons and this year’s Resident Evil , Zach Cregger has been having quite a run. We’d argue that the run started with the director’s debut movie, Barbarian. We called it “one of the wildest horror films in years” in our original 8/10 review , and it’ll be finding a new streaming home on Hulu next month.

Last but not least, it’s definitely worth keeping an eye out for Halloween specials.

Family Guy is already confirmed to be dropping its special episode on October 5, while Phineas & Ferb have a Halloween episode slated for October 7. The Simpsons will almost certainly get a new addition to its ongoing Treehouse of Horror Halloween special series on Disney+ some time later in the month. articles.title: Melissa Barrera Says She Would Reprise Her Scream Role, Reveals Conditions for Her Return
articles.summary: Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.
articles.body:
Actress Melissa Barrera said she is open to returning to Scream, but don't expect to see her reprise her role as Sam Carpenter as long as Spyglass Media has the rights.

The Scream 5 and Scream 6 star opened up about what it would take to bring her back to Wes Craven's legendary slasher franchise during an interview with JustWatch . Barrera explained that she still "loves the franchise," but the people overseeing it are what's keeping her from going another round with Ghostface.

"Not with the company that currently holds the rights," she said when asked if she would return if she got a call to reprise her role. "I love the franchise. I had an amazing time making those movies, but a lot of the hate and difficulty that I've faced in the last years is because the leadership of that company made it a point to label me something that I'm not."

"And they never apologized, even when I was proven right. Even with an apology, I wouldn't go back to work with them – not that I'm holding my breath. I don't think they have that ability."

Barrera starred in two installments for the horror franchise and was set to return for a third run with Jenna Ortega but was fired by Spyglass following a series of pro-Palestine social media posts she published in late 2023 . At the time, Spyglass said it has "zero tolerance for antisemitism or the incitement of hate."

"I pray day and night for no more deaths, for no more violence, and for peaceful co-existence," Barrera said in a statement following her firing. "I will continue to speak out for those that need it most and continue to advocate for peace and safety, for human rights and freedom. Silence is not an option for me."

The Scream rights holder's move was immediately met with backlash from fans for more reasons than one. Barrera had helped bring the franchise back to theaters after a decade without a new installment, and when she was unceremoniously removed as the lead of Scream 7 , other talent happened to follow suit. Jenna Ortega departed Scream 7 just weeks after it all went down. Director Christopher Landon confirmed his exit just one month after Spyglass fired Barrera.

Paramount Pictures and Spyglass went on to release a very different vision for the franchise when Scream 7 premiered earlier this year. Although familiar faces helped it break records at the box office , the latest entry debuted to franchise-low reviews, as shared by Rotten Tomatoes . IGN gave it a 6/10 . Scream 8 is also reportedly in the works.

Despite veering off in a completely new direction, Barrera said now that she's open to coming back. For her, it's not just about working under new management but honoring Craven's legacy.

"If the franchise were ever to leave those hands and go into hands that would, I think, honor Wes Craven's legacy more… I think, yeah," she continued regarding her interest in a return to the franchise.

For now, Barrera remains uninvolved with Scream. Series star Matthew Lillard recently spoke up about his surprise return in Scream 7. During a recent Q&A (via Deadline ), he said he was "embarrassed" to have reprised his role.

" I’m just gonna say, what happened to Melissa, the whole world didn’t pipe up," he said. "She was like a year early on what the f**k’s going on, but the whole world should have piped up and said, ‘she’s right,’ and they didn’t. And that’s brutal."

For now, Scream 8 has no release date. Although ideas for the next film are something that have been in the works behind the scenes for some time , there's no information about who may show up in it.
